summary: Iteration 10 — verified the new Audit & Activity Log feature end-to-end. Added /app/backend/tests/test_audit_logs.py (10 tests) covering admin action events (login_success, code_created/extended/revoked/deleted, limits_updated, urls_updated, emergency_stop, session_skipped), login_failed + account_locked brute-force flow, WebSocket session events (device_connected/disconnected, guest_joined, guest_active, turn_ended), category/q/pagination filtering, CSV+JSON export with correct headers, and DELETE /api/logs clearing. Full backend suite is 69/69 (existing 59 unchanged + 10 new). Frontend: dashboard Recent Activity card renders and VIEW ALL navigates to /admin/logs; the /admin/logs page renders filter bar (search/category/dates/apply), events table, and total count; category=security filter correctly excludes session badges; text search works; CSV and JSON exports trigger downloads (ossm-audit.csv / ossm-audit.json); CLEAR ALL confirm dialog + toast + refresh works (total drops to 1 = just logs_cleared); DASHBOARD back button returns to /admin.
critical_code_review_comments: log_event() correctly wraps insert in try/except so audit-log writes never break the request path — good.
log_public() explicitly drops MongoDB _id and stringifies via str(_id) into 'id' — no ObjectId serialization issue.
GET /api/logs limit is safely clamped 1..500 and skip clamped to >=0 — bounds handled.

record_failure logs account_locked with actor=identifier (contains ip+scope+email), not the raw email; the UI displays the whole identifier. Minor UX nit: consider parsing actor for account_locked/twofa_* on the Logs UI to show just the email. Not blocking.
login_failed for non-existent users is logged with the submitted (lowercased) email as actor — matches PRD intent (audit brute-force attempts).
DELETE /api/logs deletes ALL entries then writes logs_cleared → total becomes 1 immediately (consistent with 'manual clear' UX and 'total <= small' assertion).
CSV header row matches the spec exactly: 'timestamp,category,action,actor,target,detail,ip'; Content-Disposition attachment header present.
seed_data_creation: During tests a few throwaway access codes (TEST_AUDIT, TEST_WS_AUDIT, TEST_Q) were created and deleted. Test also invoked DELETE /api/logs — the audit log is now effectively empty except for events generated after that (login_success from the RecentActivity poll, and the logs_cleared marker itself). If subsequent UI verification wants a populated Recent Activity card, main agent can just log in / create a code again.
context_for_next_testing_agent: New regression file /app/backend/tests/test_audit_logs.py exercises the whole audit-log surface (logs API, filters, export, clear, plus all event-emitting endpoints and the host+guest WS lifecycle). Full backend regression command: `python -m pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml` — currently 69/69. UI selectors used: activity-log-card, view-all-logs-link, logs-page, logs-table, logs-back-button, log-total, log-search-input, log-filter-category, log-filter-start, log-filter-end, log-filter-apply, log-export-csv, log-export-json, log-clear-button, log-cat-security, log-cat-session, log-row-<action>. Note the test cleared the log; if you need pre-populated data, generate events first.
rca of the issue: No bugs found. Only test-side adjustment: my initial throwaway email used 'TEST_' uppercase, but the backend lowercases emails before storing them as the actor, so equality checks failed until I lowercased the fixture and used substring match for the account_locked actor (which is the compound identifier '<ip>:login:<email>').
